page.layout: One page of running text in a single justified column. Printed page number 116 at top left, running head DESCRIPTIO at top centre. At the foot right, below the last line, the catchword "ciorum". No marginal notes.

main_text.p: licissime à Timoleonte confecto, & Syracusarum folitudine cum nova populi frequentia, novis ibi colonis collocatis commutata, Syracusanos beneficium agnoscentes honestissimis & pulcherrimis laudibus in cœlum extulisse, per quos libertatem ac salutem adepti tyrannorum jugum, & barbarorum crudelitatem evasissent: atque has laudes cumulatas fuisse, cum Timoleon Pœnos majoribus cum copiis in Siciliam reversos, majori rursus clade castigatos tota insula expulisset, & submotis omnibus qui libertati graves erant, idem beneficium reliquis Siciliæ civitatibus universæq; insulæ, quod Syracusis, sine emolumento suo, & suorum præstitis-set. Corinthus, si Thucydidi credimus, prima civitatum Græcarum navium majorum usum novit, & maritimis rebus dedita fuit sub Bacchiadis, navali prælio cum colonis suis Corcyræis conflixit annis cc xxxii ante initium belli Peloponnesiaci, c lxxxiii ante Xerxis adventum in Græciam, Cypselo tyrannidem tenente. Ad usum maris summam commoditatem ei præstitère duo portus, de quibus dixi, Lechæus & Cen-chræus, quorum ille occidentem hic orientem spectat. Maris usus opes dedit civibus & populi frequentiâ ac ædifi-

page.notes: The text is printed in roman type with long s; all long s are transcribed as plain s. The line-end hyphen in "præstitis-set" and "ædifi-" is printed and kept. The word "præstitis-set" is as printed, though the expected form is "præstitisset". "ciorum" at the foot right is the catchword, the start of the next page's text. The numerals "cc xxxii" and "c lxxxiii" are copied as printed.
